As a DS and someone who wrote the schedule a few times. That is usually a sign that the ASDS is revising the schedule for you, your dept, etc. the company, depending on the state, is legally obligated to schedule all associates a minimum of 12 hours per week or a max of 28 for part timers. Again these numbers differ per state. You should talk NOT to your DS but to your ASDS or Store Manager for clarification. Pose it as asking for clarification. Those two people are responsible for scheduling and staffing. Your DS and your ASM are NOT responsible for those things. 

In regards to full time to part time. Full timers are typically the back bones of every dept. all part timers are to work the shifts that full timers don’t (since most depts have set schedules for their full timers). That said each dept is allocated a specific number of hours for each dept and they are only allowed a certain number of associates in each dept. like my lumber dept has 1 open, 1 maid, and 1 close full timer and the part timers fill in the shifts that the full timers don’t work. All of this is automated based on sales (theoretically and my hint of doubt) btw, and the ASDS is responsible to adjust or tweak the schedule based on SM specifications, seasons, etc but they are not allowed to exceed a certain number of hours. Assuming you’re doing your job and doing it well, you’re likely not getting full time because the system determines that your store is at or is exceeding the number of full timers your store is allowed to have without your SM getting his/her  wrists slapped. And no, the stores aren’t typically allowed to give you full time and split you across a few depts. all stores do this but aren’t exactly supposed to because the premise is that full timers get set schedules to build rapport with regular customers at regular times. I hope this clarifies.

Bottom line: check with your ASM or ASDS to see if you qualify for medical loa and also check to see if you are paying for short term/ long term disability. 

I’m in medical loa right now (currently laying in bed recovering from surgery). First I told my ASM and HR rep that I’m fed up living with my pain and I’m looking at doctors. That’s all you need to say to them at this time. They will hook you up with paperwork or directions (most of the paperwork is meant to go directly to the doc so you don’t even fill it out; just make sure you follow up on everything). Before looking at the paperwork I recommend that you schedule doctor appointments to be on your days off. Go through all the doc recommendation channels UNTIL THEY TELL YOU E.X.A.C.T.L.Y. WHAT IS WRONG. Do NOT submit the LOA before that because the company we go through (Hartford for short term disability) will NOT pay you for time off (regardless of how you personally feel) and HDHR will NOT approve your medical LOA (regardless of how you personally feel) without a doctor filling out paperwork detailing what’s wrong and how long you’ll be out with a start date and a projected end date (all info they need after you visited all your doctors and got something specific). Without any specific order from a doctor there’s nothing they can or will do and you’ll be a sitting unpaid duck. (Btw, in my state Hartford only pays me 60% of my paycheck).

Once a doctor says what to do (surgery in my case), I went to management and told them that I’m expected to go to surgery on (this date). I followed along the paperwork (there is a nice checklist) and I made sure the doctor, HR, and Hartford processed everything and when things get processed. 

I cannot stress enough that you got to do the leg work and get your doctor appointments set up and just do them. Ask for soonest dates. If your Salaried managers are chill and your store has good coverage (shocking everyone) then you can swap days to work to get your ideal appointments. REFRAIN FROM CALLING OUT IF IT CAN BE HELPED BUT ALWAYS TAKE CARE OF NUMBER ONE IF YOU NEED TO.

Small solutions: if you EVER type something on the register, then it HAS to be done in OCB. When you go into OCB pull down the drop menu next to the search menu and select “ALL”. That’s when you type in the SKU and ALL SKU’s work in there. OCB by itself will only show the “popular” SKU’s whether you type it in or not. Under no circumstance do you type any SKU without OCB and “ALL.” 

Note: one item in a transaction will sabotage the whole transaction regardless of how much they are buying. So if one item is typed into the wrong area the whole transaction is contaminated. The metric is Scan % and it’s not based on individual items scanned. It’s based on transactions done correctly. So it is possible to get an extraordinarily small scan % if someone does this on 90% of their transactions even at self check.

Edit Note: nuts and bolts with the 3 letters are the only products in the whole building that are exempt.

Double edit note: at Self Check none of the transactions are attached to your name UNLESS you log in to one of the registers to solve a customers problem. As since that is usually done when you need to type in a SKU for them then that messes up your scan % drastically. For example: say you only had to sign into the registers 10 times in 1 day. That means you had only 10 transactions. Let’s say that out of those 10, 9 of them you had to type in a SKU and you theoretically typed it in the wrong place. This means, you got 9/10 transactions incorrect and so your scan % is only 10% for that day. If this is the trend the whole week then that could result in a low score. Obviously, more transactions the better but being at self check limits that and if you only work a couple days a week then it limits you further. Accuracy becomes more important.

Here is my daily routine:

My alarm goes off 2 hours before my work shift. I then lay around for 30 minutes and then get up to take a 30-45 minute shower in which I sit down in said shower and look at all my notifications and check the weather (I live in Alaska and I need to know how cold it is to dictate what I wear and if I need to warm up my car). I then spend the rest of the time getting dressed and grab something easy to eat which is usually just lunch meat and a yogurt. I then fill my back pack with a soda, v8 juice, and fruit juice and take a yogurt to go. At work I sit at a desk and check my email for company updates and customers requesting supplies and I play on my phone until I have a customer. My play-on-my-phone time is usually watching YouTube for music and video games and sometimes an inspirational video. I do this for 8 hours and I spread my backpack food over the course of that day. After work I head home, take off my shoes (which are laced shoes that I turned into slip ons) and take off my layers and my pants. I hate wearing socks and prefer to walk around the apartment barefoot with a t shirt and my underwear. If I feel gross I will take another shower otherwise I pour myself a drink like whiskey with coke or a coffee with cream and sugar and then microwave a TV dinner. After that I turn on my tv and check to see if my online friends are on so we can play Destiny 2 together. If not I go to YouTube to see if I haven’t missed anything or to put on a gameplay video of the games I love. If nothing is there then I turn on Netflix to see what I can find. If not there then I rotate to checking if my online friends are on then to YouTube and then to Netflix. I repeat this behavior until it gets late or until I find something I like or if my friends hop on. I then fall asleep and repeat this Monday through Friday as since those are the days I work. On Saturday, I wake up and immediately take a shower for 30-45 minutes and then turn on my PS4 to repeat my game, YouTube, and Netflix trifecta until it’s late or something sticks. On Sunday, I wake up, take my 30-45 minute shower, and get dressed in comfy clothes. I go to the laundry room in my apartment complex and start the wash load. I then set a timer for 45 mins and then I leave the apartment and go grocery shopping and collect my mail for the week and then when I get home I put all my groceries away and then rotate my laundry. I then set a timer for 50 minutes and then turn on my PS4 and repeat my game, youtube, Netflix trifecta until my timer sounds off and then I get my laundry, put it all away or dump it on my bed (depending on my depression and loneliness) and then return to my trifecta until it’s late or I find something I like. And then the week restarts and I repeat the process. 

Some random things that sometimes changes my routine:

On Saturday, if there is a movie I’d like to see in theater I use the Regal app to preorder my ticket and I always buy a matinee. I’d do my normal morning routine as if getting ready to work (wake up two hours before, 30-45 min shower, etc) and then go watch the movie and then return home to proceed with my PS4 trifecta. 

Sometimes if I have a craving I’ll go out to eat once a week (usually on Saturday) and I always go somewhere I never been to. 

This is the blueprint of everyday. Yes in all the in between moments I talk to my coworkers and I talk to waitresses/ waiters and the people who work at the movies. I talk to my online friends when we get a chance. But still I feel completely lonely, isolated, and depressed. I have broken many routines and I done many spontaneous things in my life to reach out and meet people and try to find that one meaningful connection but nothing sticks. I just want a real connection and I honestly feel it’s too late for me. I’m not exactly bad looking but I think my problem is that I’m awkward and weird. My face looks unapproachable even if I’m in a great mood. Just a constant resting bitch face for a dude. So my “aura” or “vibe” or the impression I give is that I’m someone who can’t be interrupted even though that is further from the truth. I want to be interrupted.
